issue_context.title: ipaddr_to_asc() added to 3.0.0 incorrectly formats IPv6 addresses
issue_context.body:
Function `ipaddr_to_asc` in `crypto/x509/v3_utl.c` converts a 4 or 16 octet value to an IPv4 or IPv6 address text represenation. What was noticed while testing Perl Net::SSLeay with OpenSSL 3.0.0 alpha5 and later is that `ipaddr_to_asc` text representation is incorrect with IPv6. The latest OpenSSL 1.1.1 and earlier work as expected, as shown below. The problem seems to have appeared during 3.0.0 development.

The example below is from an up-to-date macOS Catalina and Apple Xcode compilers.  I'd say this is not related to any particular platform.
```
% cc -v
Apple clang version 11.0.3 (clang-1103.0.32.29)
Target: x86_64-apple-darwin19.6.0
Thread model: posix
InstalledDir: /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin
% uname -a
Darwin imac-retina.local 19.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 19.6.0: Sun Jul  5 00:43:10 PDT 2020; root:xnu-6153.141.1~9/RELEASE_X86_64 x86_64
```
This shows output with OpenSSL 1.1.1g that was compiled today:
```
% openssl version                                                                                            
OpenSSL 1.1.1g  21 Apr 2020
% openssl x509 -in t/data/testcert_extended.crt.pem -noout -text |grep -A1 'X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:'
            X509v3 Subject Alternative Name: 
                email:alt1@email.com, Registered ID:1.2.3.4.5, URI:http://name.dom.com/whatever, DNS:dns.name.com, IP Address:10.11.12.13, othername:<unsupported>, IP Address:2A00:1450:4001:C01:0:0:0:93
```
This shows output with OpenSSL master checked out and compiled today:
```
% openssl version                                                                                            
OpenSSL 3.0.0-alpha7-dev  (Library: OpenSSL 3.0.0-alpha7-dev )
% openssl x509 -in t/data/testcert_extended.crt.pem -noout -text |grep -A1 'X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:'
            X509v3 Subject Alternative Name: 
                email:alt1@email.com, Registered ID:1.2.3.4.5, URI:http://name.dom.com/whatever, DNS:dns.name.com, IP Address:10.11.12.13, othername: 1.2.3.4.5::othername, IP Address:2A0145400C010:
```

comments:
`out += 3` just looks wrong here:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/2a33470b4f23bcf1cd66bbf645c855142efa0ed9/crypto/x509/v3_utl.c#L988-L994

We're writing potentially 5 characters of output, but incrementing 3 each time!? Also the output width is variable. Possible fixes are to use a fixed width format specifier, or to check the return value of BIO_snprintf to check what was actually written.

@DDvO
That loop was...  something.  I've a tentative fix in #12696, please try it out.

I built from your fix branch and it looks as expected. The address is now exactly identical to what 1.1.1g prints out:

```
% openssl version
OpenSSL 3.0.0-alpha7-dev  (Library: OpenSSL 3.0.0-alpha7-dev )
% openssl x509 -in t/data/testcert_extended.crt.pem -noout -text |grep -A1 'X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:'
            X509v3 Subject Alternative Name: 
                email:alt1@email.com, Registered ID:1.2.3.4.5, URI:http://name.dom.com/whatever, DNS:dns.name.com, IP Address:10.11.12.13, othername: 1.2.3.4.5::othername, IP Address:2A00:1450:4001:C01:0:0:0:93
```

review_comments:
I suggest keeping an explicit NUL termination just in case `BIO_snprintf()` failed (indicated by `bytes < 0`)
because in this case I fear that it is not guaranteed that the string is properly terminated:
`buf[out - bytes] = '\0';`

In case the `BIO_printf()` output was truncated according to the buffer limit it would return `remain`, which would terminate the loop (and thus the output string) prematurely, 
but this cannot happen because the buffer is surely large enough.
Do you see the comment above the buffer?  In IPv6 address will be a maximum of 39 characters (bytes in this case) when written out, so there's absolutely enough space for the terminating NUL byte.

Yes, but as I wrote (according to the man page of `snprintf` etc., so likely also holds for `BIO_snprintf`):
On potential truncation (not possible here), the function will return `reminder`,
and on an output error it returns a negative value.
And unfortunately the documentation is not really clear (at least to me) whether the string is properly terminated in such (non-success) cases.
Yet we may be safe here because for string output no output error can occur.
